posts: Every wallet onboarding still makes users memorize 12 words before they've done a single thing. Seed phrase first, value later is backwards UX. Prove the app is useful, then hand over the keys. #wallets

Chain signatures should mean you sign once in the wallet you already trust and the tx lands wherever it needs to. If your dapp still makes me switch networks mid-flow, that's not abstraction, that's a detour. #chainsignatures #near

replies.text: Adoption tracks UX more than liquidity imo. Nobody picks a chain off a roadmap; they stay where signing doesn't feel like paperwork. Make chain signatures invisible and the cycle matters less.
Learning you lost 1.6% to IL after the fact is a wallet UX bug. Confirm screens should simulate IL at ±10% chop before you sign, not let the dashboard break the news a week later.
